subject.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose `compat.disableBoundaryAwareCache` and auto-enable it for DeepSeek, or should the cache repair remain an internal provider-specific rule without a new public compatibility field?
rationale: The cache regression and implementation are well supported, but choosing a permanent exported config/default contract—and accepting trailing instruction-message semantics—requires repository owner intent rather than reviewer inference.

options.title: Sponsor the current contract
options.body: Approve the public compatibility field, DeepSeek automatic default, explicit false opt-out, and trailing instruction carrier, then reopen or land this PR after normal gates.

options.title: Narrow the repair
options.body: Keep the DeepSeek cache fix but remove the generic public field, implementing the behavior as a provider-owned internal default until another prefix-matching provider has contract evidence.

options.title: Keep boundary-aware behavior
options.body: Decline the alternate request shaping and keep the PR closed, documenting the current DeepSeek cost limitation and any supported operator workaround.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the current contract
recommendation.body: Approve the public compatibility field, DeepSeek automatic default, explicit false opt-out, and trailing instruction carrier, then reopen or land this PR after normal gates.

likelyOwner.reason: The prompt-cache boundary and stability behavior appears to date primarily to their merged feature work, and GitHub identifies them as a repository member on that surface.
